newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam keen on Ho Chi Minh Trail expressway plan.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam keen on Ho Chi Minh Trail expressway plan.

text.p: Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet is keen for work to begin next year on turning stretches of the wartime Ho Chi Minh Trail into a north-south expressway, the Saigon Times Daily said on Wednesday.
The newspaper said Kiet, who has called for a mass labour programme to build the 1,800-km (1,125-mile) road, wanted a project feasibility study completed by the end of this year.

However, he appeared to have rowed back on his original ambition for a new trunk road down the west side of the Truong Son mountains which would have cost some $6 billion -- equivalent to more than a quarter of the country's annual national income.
"The prime minister admitted...that the highway will be set up based on the upgrading of the Ho Chi Minh Trail and the National Highway Number 14," it said.
Hanoi's communist forces built the twisting and turning trail from a maze of jungle tracks to funnel weapons, supplies and troops to the U.S.-backed South Vietnam during the war which ended in 1975.

Although no one disputes the need for Vietnam's crumbling infrastructure to be revamped, both local and foreign analysts have questioned the economic sense of drafting millions of workers to build the new road.
Hanoi has had a compulsory labour programme for many years under which young people are required to contribute 10 days' work each year or pay an exemption fee.

But the government last month announced plans to breathe new life into the programme by expanding the age group of participants and allowing individual provincial or city authorities to set their own exemption fees.

The government lashed out at international news broadcasters for their coverage of the new labour drive, dubbing their reports slanderous, and has adopted rousing nationalistic rhetoric to highlight its merits.
"I think the romanticism (of voluntary work) has not yet disappeared," Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth League official Nguyen Thanh Phong told the Tuoi Tre newspaper on Tuesday.
"The city's youth is always ready to go into the forests and down to the sea," he said. "So participation in industrialising the Truong Son trail is a great opportunity for us."
